comments.body:
## Summary of work on $(\star)$: $1/\Phi_n(p\boxp q) \ge 1/\Phi_n(p)+1/\Phi_n(q)$

I reviewed the existing solution, verified its correct parts, **found and corrected a genuine error in its central "reduction"**, and **proved a new sharp inequality that yields a complete proof of a substantial new case** (one factor Gaussian, all $n$). The general conjecture remains open, so I am marking this **in_progress** (not resolved).

### Proved rigorously and unconditionally
1. Closed form $\Phi_n(p)=\sum_{i\ne j}(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^{-2}$.
2. **Score-Laplacian identities (new):** with PSD weighted Laplacian $(Lv)_i=\sum_{j\ne i}(v_i-v_j)/(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)^2$: $L\lambda=s$, $\Phi_n=\langle s,s\rangle$, $I=2\langle s,Ls\rangle$, $\langle\lambda,s\rangle=\langle\lambda,L\lambda\rangle=n(n-1)/2$.
3. Covariance/identity (cleaned up a hand-wavy step using $(x-c)^n=e^{-c\partial}x^n$).
4. Heat semigroup $p\boxp G_t=e^{-(t/2)\partial^2}p$, $G_s\boxp G_t=G_{s+t}$, $\Phi_n(G_t)=\frac{n(n-1)}{4t}$ (fixed a garbled derivation of $\sum h_i^2=n(n-1)$).
5. Root velocity = score; exact de Bruijn $\frac{d}{dt}\Phi_n(p_t)=-I(p_t)\le0$.
6. $n=2$ equality.

### Main new result: sharp finite-free Cramér–Rao/Stam bound
$$I(p)\ \ge\ \frac{4}{n(n-1)}\Phi_n(p)^2,\qquad g(p)=I/\Phi_n^2\ge\tfrac{4}{n(n-1)},$$
equality iff $p$ is a scaled/translated Hermite. **Proof:** Cauchy–Schwarz for $\langle u,v\rangle_L=\langle u,Lv\rangle$: $\langle\lambda,Ls\rangle^2\le\langle\lambda,L\lambda\rangle\langle s,Ls\rangle$, with LHS $=\Phi_n^2$ (as $L\lambda=s$) and RHS $=\frac{n(n-1)}{2}\cdot\frac I2$. Numerically $\min_p g=4/(n(n-1))$ exactly for $n=2..7$.

### Consequence: complete proof of $(\star)$ against a Gaussian factor, ALL $n$
$\psi(u)=\frac1{\Phi_n(p\boxp G_u)}-\frac1{\Phi_n(p)}-\frac1{\Phi_n(G_u)}$ has $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi'(u)=g(p\boxp G_u)-\frac{4}{n(n-1)}\ge0$, hence $\psi\ge0$. So $(\star)$ holds whenever $q=G_t$ (strict unless $p$ Hermite). Verified, 0 failures over thousands of instances.

### Correction of the earlier "reduction" (important)
The previous solution reduced $(\star)$ to an "infinitesimal Stam" inequality (S) along a coupled heat flow as "the one remaining lemma." **That reduction is vacuous:** (S) is feasible with nonneg speeds iff $g(R)\le\max(g(P),g(Q))$, and I found reachable states (including $t=0$ with genuine $p,q$) where $g(R)>\max(g(P),g(Q))$ — e.g. $n=4$: $g(p)\approx0.615,\ g(q)\approx0.572,\ g(p\boxp q)\approx0.829$. So heat-flow coupling alone cannot prove $(\star)$. That section was rewritten honestly.

### Honest status
$(\star)$ holds in all $>2\times10^4$ random tests ($2\le n\le5$); equality is approached exactly as one factor $\to$ Gaussian, matching the new theorem. The general case is equivalent to $\Phi_n(r)\le\Phi_n(p)\Phi_n(q)/(\Phi_n(p)+\Phi_n(q))$ and reduces to a **finite-free score-projection lemma** (express $\score(p\boxp q)$ as a norm-nonincreasing affine combination of $\score(p),\score(q)$). This remains **open**.

All identities/inequalities checked numerically; solution.tex rewritten. Marking **in_progress**.
